name: tag_write

inputBounds.hardItemsPolicyRule: a deployment may raise the 20-item default through the Runtime Target Policy and never above the 100-item hard ceiling
inputBounds.numericInputBytes: a boolean counts as 5 bytes, an integer as its decimal width (a bit-length upper bound, never its text), and any other number as 32 bytes
inputBounds.countingRule: every count is incremental and stops at the ceiling or at the aggregate budget it is checked against, so a reported byte amount is a lower bound; an integer is counted from its width and never converted to be measured; the aggregate walk measures each item against the budget left for it and refuses as soon as that is crossed, so a later item's ceiling is never scanned after the refusal point

nativeOutcome: system.tag.writeBlocking QualityCode per item; observed state does not decide success

runtimeTargetPolicy.allowlistMatch: provider-qualified prefix at segment boundaries; explicit * allows every provider
runtimeTargetPolicy.reservedProviderRefusal: permission_denied before Preflight, whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *

preflight: input, reserved provider and Target allowlist for every item before any item executes, with no rollback
deniedMutationAudit: after a usable Policy is read, a refused target produces one `decision` row and no dispatch; `off` records nothing, and `required` refuses the call when the denial row cannot be written
outcomePreservation: a dispatched batch reports its per-item Native outcomes whatever the Observed-state budget or the serializer does; the Observed budget is decided by one bounded walk that both measures and renders (a Dataset through its column names and cells, a list or a Java array through every member with a separator charged to each, a string with its quotes and JSON escapes, and a number from its width instead of its text, all under a 16-level nesting depth and an incremental count that stops at the budget), so nothing is materialized before its cost is inside the budget; the timestamp is measured by the same walk against what the value left, an Observed value or entry that cannot be returned is an explicit `limit_exceeded` observed error stating the counted size, the width bound or the depth reached, and the result is re-rendered without the Observed state rather than replacing the outcomes
nativeOutcomeText: `code` and `good` are always exact; a `name` or `level` over its ceiling is omitted (null) with `nameOverLimitBytes`/`levelOverLimitBytes` reporting the counted size, because a truncated identifier would assert one the provider never reported; the free-text `diagnosticMessage` is a bounded 512-byte prefix with `diagnosticMessageOverLimitBytes` marking it. Every count is incremental and stops at its budget, so a marker is exact for any text within 8192 bytes and a lower bound beyond it.
itemOutcomeUnknownScope: only items whose native outcome is itself indeterminate
